solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hymn may be amusing when king is deposed

parts.note: may and can both express being able or allowed

indicators.note: a deposed monarch is removed from office, so the king's letter is removed

parts.note: to tickle is to amuse, so to be amusing to someone is to tickle them
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A solemn hymn might become funny once the monarch has been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deposed' takes K out of TICKLE, leaving TICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a song or chant taken from the Bible, sung in church services.

clue.text: Composers modern and ancient — the latter heard canary?

parts.note: John Cage was a modern American composer

indicators.note: the second of the two composers is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: William Byrd was a Tudor composer, ancient beside Cage

explanation.surface: A musical riddle about pairing a modern and an old composer, hinting at a singing pet.
explanation.walkthrough: BYRD sounds like BIRD. The question mark marks canary as only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A canary is a classic example of a songbird kept indoors in a cage.

clue.text: Girl that is abandoned at birth

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: Natalie is a girl's name
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A grim story of a girl left as a foundling the moment she was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective for anything relating to birth, as in prenatal care.

clue.text: Now and again stay hidden in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Advice to lie low every so often among some ruined buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and again' looks like one phrase meaning occasionally; split it, 'Now' is the definition and 'and' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the present era, the modern times we live in.

clue.text: One boy in Lyon, not on shore leave

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the shortened city name
not here means without, so the word on is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
Bert is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lone young man in the French city of Lyon who isn't allowed time ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' turns LYON into LY, and 'in' puts IBERT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty is naval slang for permission granted to sailors to go ashore for a short time.

clue.text: Traditionally they're beaten in spring (and summer originally)

parts.note: to spring is to leap, to bound

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the word's opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Something customarily beaten in springtime, and in summer too.
explanation.walkthrough: Beating the bounds is an old English parish custom of walking the boundary at Rogationtide, in spring, and striking the markers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounds are limits or borders, which parishioners traditionally walked round and struck with sticks.

clue.text: Fast ships reached young son at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A young son who has been reached while out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to fast passenger liners on the Atlantic, likened to racing dogs.

clue.text: With grandmother and father, I have to climb a mountain

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
dad means father

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the letters upwards, back to front

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A family expedition: with Gran and Dad, I've got to scale a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns IVE into EVI. Nanda Devi is a peak in the Indian Himalaya.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanda Devi is the second-highest peak in India, in the Garhwal Himalaya.

clue.text: Light piece of furniture

definitions.meaning: to light is to alight, come to rest, as a bird does on a branch
a long wooden bench with a high back and arms

explanation.surface: A lightweight item of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as an adjective describing the furniture but is a verb, to come down and rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird lands and comes to rest; separately, the word names a high-backed wooden bench.

clue.text: Old police sergeant's first arrest

parts.note: the Stasi was the East German secret police

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: The first arrest made by a sergeant in the old East German police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrest' looks like a police action, but here it is a noun meaning a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of standstill, and an arrest is a stopping of motion or growth.

clue.text: About time animal is nobbled

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the animal's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: a goat is an animal

explanation.surface: A racing tale of an animal interfered with just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal for tampered with or bribed, as a racehorse or juror may be.

clue.text: Tree, say, hugged by British eccentric

indicators.note: something hugged by others is held inside them

parts.note: a nut is a crank or eccentric person
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A tree, perhaps, being embraced by an odd British tree-hugger.
explanation.definitionFit: The butternut is a North American walnut tree with oily edible nuts.

clue.text: Evil One stopping poet's game

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the pieces fill the middle of the other word

parts.note: a bard is a poet; with the 's it gives BARDS
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Devil putting a stop to a poet's game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil One' looks like a name for Satan but splits into ILL and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue sport played on a cloth-covered table with balls and pockets.

clue.text: Irishman back home meeting everyone

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: in means at home
everyone means all

explanation.surface: An Irishman returns home and greets everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Niall is a traditional Irish man's name, as in Niall of the Nine Hostages.

clue.text: Time to be off: vagrant strayed

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A tramp drifted off because it was time to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to be off' suggests leaving, but means a day off work.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of rest is a day away from work, so it is time to be off duty.

clue.text: Accepts unusual French article that's visually striking

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: Someone takes on an odd French object that catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking public display or sight, something impressive to look at.

clue.text: Acolyte is cut off crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so the other letters go over and around the river

parts.note: to sever is to cut off

explanation.surface: An altar boy is stranded when he crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte assists the priest at Mass, a role also called an altar server.

clue.text: Animals extremely ruminative, certainly, not quite right

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outer letters are used
not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: indeed means certainly

explanation.surface: Some cud-chewing animals that are certainly a bit off.
explanation.definitionFit: These are deer of the Arctic, called caribou in North America, and they chew the cud.

clue.text: Copper reported cheers

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the letters are taken as they sound

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer said thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal, symbol Cu, which said as two letters sounds like a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British use cheers is an informal goodbye, like a casual farewell.

clue.text: Turn up after relative almost gets clear

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
almost means not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read upwards, back to front

parts.note: a go is a turn

explanation.surface: A relative shows up and nearly gets the all-clear.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclog a drain or pipe is to clear the blockage from it.

clue.text: Crazy festival venue found by conductor?

parts.note: Hay-on-Wye, a Welsh border town, hosts a famous literary festival
a wire conducts electricity

explanation.surface: A mad festival location discovered by an orchestra's conductor?
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests a maestro but is an electrical conductor. Hay is Hay-on-Wye, a town in Wales known for its book festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire is an idiom for behaving erratically, out of control.

clue.text: Percy is in demand on branch line

parts.note: something hot is popular or sought after
a spur is a short branch railway line

explanation.surface: Percy is popular on a local railway branch line.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Percy, nicknamed Harry Hotspur, is the rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Percy was the fiery medieval nobleman known by this nickname.

clue.text: Artificially produced waterfall at head of dale

parts.note: force is a northern English word for a waterfall, as in Aira Force

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man-made waterfall at the top of a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A force, from Old Norse, is a waterfall in the Lake District and Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced plants, or forced laughter, are brought on unnaturally rather than in the normal way.

clue.text: Moderate beheaded in many cases

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: to moderate is to soften

explanation.surface: A moderate is executed in many instances.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens frequently occurs on many occasions.

clue.text: A plant that's cultivated like this gets new twigs

parts.note: cotton is a widely cultivated plant
so means thus, like this

explanation.surface: A garden plant grown in a certain way produces fresh shoots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twigs' suggests shoots but is a verb, as in to twig a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for coming to understand something, catching on.

clue.text: Arab, retaining uranium, depressed leader in Iran

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside

parts.note: depressed means sad
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: leader in means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Arab holding uranium, and a downcast leader in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Saudi Arabia is an Arab of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Put up with a band on cloud nine

parts.note: to cock is to put up or raise, as a dog cocks an ear
a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: Tolerating a band while feeling elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but splits into COCK and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for being extremely happy and pleased with oneself.

clue.text: Putting name to river is futile

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Naming a river is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile is pointless, of no help or purpose.

clue.text: Engine driver stops working with European line

parts.note: a machine dies when it stops working

explanation.surface: A train driver halts work with a European railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engine driver' suggests a train driver but means the fuel that drives an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is the oil fuel that powers compression-ignition motors.

clue.text: Harriet's novel is cheaper

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Harriet's book is a cheaper product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy means of poor quality and cheap, so the comparative means cheaper and nastier.
